:::{#thm-chain-vec}
#### Vector chain rule

Let $\vx$ be a $p \times 1$ vector,
let $\vy = \vec{g}(\vx)$ be a $q \times 1$ vector-valued function of $\vx$,
and let $z = f(\vy)$ be a scalar-valued function of $\vy$,
where $\vec{g}$ and $f$ have continuous partial derivatives.
Then $z = f(\vec{g}(\vx))$, as a function of $\vx$, satisfies

$$
\underbrace{\derivf{z}{\vx}}_{p \times 1}
= \underbrace{\derivf{\vy}{\vx}}_{p \times q}
\underbrace{\derivf{z}{\vy}}_{q \times 1}
$$

where $\derivf{\vy}{\vx}$ is the derivative of @def-vector-valued-derivative
and $\derivf{z}{\vx}$ and $\derivf{z}{\vy}$ are vector derivatives (@def-vector-derivative).

:::
